provenance.note: Envelope lists the registered upstreams; every fact carries its own citation (source_label/source_url/data_date, migrated to per-record sources), including one-off documents (1886 lease indenture, court reports) not registrable as living sources.

note: Hand-curated Madurai water facts. v1 - replaces with dynamic fact-builder when M3 data layers (CPCB river quality, ward profiles, satellite GEE) ship.

facts.title: MMC sanctioned drinking-water draw
facts.interpretation: Madurai Municipal Corporation's sanctioned annual drinking-water allocation from Vaigai Dam, the operational source for the city. Headroom over current draw means structural supply room; the constraint today is treatment capacity, not raw water.

facts.title: MMC current annual draw
facts.interpretation: Current actual annual drinking-water draw from Vaigai, ~600 Mcft/year below the 1,500 Mcft sanctioned allocation. The gap is structural - Pannaipatty WTP's design capacity caps treated supply at 125 MLD.

facts.title: Pannaipatty WTP design capacity
facts.interpretation: Pannaipatty Water Treatment Plant is the only treatment facility for Madurai's Vaigai supply. The Mullai Periyar dedicated supply scheme (under construction) is designed to lift treated capacity to 250 MLD, closing the gap to the 2034 design demand of ~250 MLD for ~1.7M residents.

facts.title: Vaigai Dam capacity
facts.interpretation: The headline reservoir for Madurai city, 6,143 Mcft at 71 ft full reservoir level, commissioned in 1959 by then-CM K. Kamaraj. Hydroelectric capacity added 1990.

facts.title: Mullaperiyar Dam storage cap
facts.interpretation: Two reference levels for the same dam. Kerala caps storage at 142 ft per Supreme Court 2014 ruling; TN-side records preserve the historical 152 ft FRL. Vaigai gets ~80% of its inflow from Mullaperiyar via the trans-basin Periyar tunnel.

facts.title: Mullaperiyar lease deed
facts.interpretation: 1886 Periyar Lake Lease Indenture between the Maharaja of Travancore and the Secretary of State for India in Council. Still in force; subject of ongoing Kerala-TN dispute since 1979 safety concerns.

facts.title: Madurai West block status
facts.interpretation: Draft-to-availability ratio of 105.8% in CGWB's 2024 Dynamic Groundwater Resource Assessment - above the 100% threshold, meaning extraction exceeds annual recharge. Usilampatti is critical at 95.0%; three blocks (Madurai South, Vadipatti, Peraiyur) are semi-critical 70-90%.

facts.title: GWR2024 blocks classified
facts.interpretation: Madurai East/West/North/South + 7 peri-urban blocks. 1 over-exploited, 1 critical, 3 semi-critical, 6 safe.

facts.title: CGWB monitoring stations
facts.interpretation: CGWB / TN-NHP / TN State GW network across Madurai district. Of these, 21 are CGWB Year Book observation wells with published quarterly hydrographs and 4 are India-WRIS live telemetric stations; the remainder are seasonal manual points. Madurai has no MMC ward-level piezometer mesh comparable to Chennai's CMWSSB 200-station network.

facts.title: Fully-lost urban tanks
facts.interpretation: Combined ~16.5 sq km lost (~30% of city). Madurai Corporation offices stand on Tallakulam tank's bed; the District Court complex on Sengulam tank's bed. 15,000+ slum households now live on former tank beds.

facts.title: Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam
facts.interpretation: Built by Thirumalai Nayak; the largest temple tank in Tamil Nadu / South India at 305m × 290m (~16 acres). Fed by an underground channel from Vaigai. The Thai float festival held annually. Restored 2017-2020.

facts.title: Anaikondan / Arittapatti BHS
facts.interpretation: Notified November 2022 - Tamil Nadu's first Biodiversity Heritage Site, 193.2 hectares around Anaikondan tank in Tirumangalam taluk. The kanmoi network here is Pandyan-era (16th century).

facts.title: Thenkal Kanmoi (Thirupparankundram)
facts.interpretation: 377 acres, 107 Mcft capacity, fed by Vaigai dam via the Nilaiyur canal. Reported completely dry in August 2025. Subject of HC PIL R. Manibharathi v UoI (WP(M) 31214/2023).

facts.title: HC water-body registry order
facts.interpretation: Madras HC Madurai bench (R. Manibharathi v UoI) directed TN to publish a public website listing every water body with survey number, location, original and present extent within 6 months. Petition filed over Thenkal Kanmoi and Vandiyur tank bund-road encroachment.

facts.title: City STP capacity
facts.interpretation: Three reported Madurai STPs - Avaniyapuram (~54-125 MLD), Sakkimangalam (45.7 MLD), and Vandiyur. MMC's sewerage pages do not publish plant-level capacities, so these figures come from news and CPCB references and are not yet officially confirmed. Set against an estimated city demand of ~270 MLD, they point to on the order of ~100 MLD of untreated discharge into the Vaigai-Kruthumal system.

facts.title: Vaigai discharge points (Madras HC, 2024)
facts.interpretation: In December 2024 the Madras High Court Madurai bench took suo motu cognisance of Vaigai pollution. Court submissions reported in the press flagged 177 sewage and industrial discharge points across the five districts the river crosses, with sampled stretches graded unfit even for irrigation. The Additional Advocate General admitted sewage mixing; a state action plan was ordered. Figures are from press-reported submissions; the underlying TNPCB report is not yet public.
facts.source_label: Madras HC Madurai Bench (suo motu) via DT Next

facts.title: Borewells chasing a falling water table
facts.interpretation: Along Madurai's flagship surviving tank network, borewell depths deepened from roughly 8 m in the early 1990s to 60 m by 2007 and about 200 m by 2017-18, as the shallow aquifer was drawn down and recharge from the broken tank cascade dwindled. The Madurai West block is now over-exploited at 105.8% draft-to-recharge (CGWB 2024).
facts.source_label: Sashikkumar et al., Discover Applied Sciences (2020)

facts.title: MMC Vaigai cleanup proposal
facts.interpretation: Madurai Municipal Corporation submitted a Rs 440 crore proposal in 2024 covering pumping-station overhaul plus Vaigai river cleanup. Submitted to TN govt; status: pending sanction.

facts.title: MMC ward count
facts.interpretation: Madurai Municipal Corporation has 100 wards across 5 zones (Central, East, North, South, West). Upgraded from 72 wards in 2011. A proposed expansion to 120 wards is not yet operational.

facts.title: Madurai daily water supply
facts.interpretation: MMC's reported daily supply across its schemes (23 + 2 + 68 + 54.7 MLD): Vaigai direct draw, Mullaperiyar augmentation, AMRUT scheme, and city distribution, treated at the Pannaipatty plant. This is the utility's stated daily delivery; the ADB TNUFIP IEE accounts total installed scheme capacity at 192 MLD, the gap reflecting derated/non-functional sources and distribution losses.

facts.title: Vaigai dam annual allocation to Madurai
facts.interpretation: Madurai is sanctioned 1,500 mcft per year from Vaigai Dam. Current draw is 900 mcft - 60% of the allocation. The constraint is pumping and treatment capacity, not water rights.

facts.title: Piped water connections in Madurai
facts.interpretation: 91,620 domestic + 4,067 commercial + 361 industrial connections across the 100-ward MMC area. Updates the 87,091 figure from the 2010-11 city handbook - net growth of ~9,000 connections in 15 years.

facts.title: Madurai overhead reservoirs
facts.interpretation: 23 overhead reservoirs hold 34.85 MLD of treated water city-wide, supplemented by one ground-level reservoir at 6.80 MLD. Distribution flows through 467 km of mains across 12 service zones.

facts.title: City-operated borewells
facts.interpretation: MMC operates 2,850 borewells across the city to supplement piped supply, alongside 3,863 public fountains. Borewell-fed supply is part of why Madurai West block is over-exploited (105.8% draft-to-availability per CGWB 2024).

facts.title: Underground sewerage length
facts.interpretation: 206.09 km of underground sewer plus 165 km of open drainage. The British laid the first UGD in 1924 (covering ~30% of today's footprint); JNNURM extended it to ~90% of households by 2011. Open drains carry the rest, often into the seven named historic surplus channels that now function as sewage outlets.

facts.title: Sewer pumping stations
facts.interpretation: Nine main pumping stations in the south zone (Santhapettai, Thavittusandhai, Melavasal, West Market-Canara Bank, Sunday Market, Karukagapillai Kara Lane, Thaikkal, Puttuthoppu, Arapalayam-New) and five in the north zone (Mundiri Thoppu, Thathaneri, K.K. Nagar, Anna Nagar, Anna Nagar Uzhvar Sandhai-New).

facts.title: Vaigai Riverfront Development project
facts.interpretation: Smart City Mission project: counter-fort retaining walls, walkways, greenbelt, ghats, lighting, e-toilets, children's play areas. Distinct from the Rs 440 crore Vaigai cleanup proposal (pumping-station overhaul + river cleanup, submitted 2024, pending TN sanction). The riverfront project beautifies the bank; it does not address the sand-mining bed-drop that severed the cascade.

facts.title: Over-exploited groundwater blocks (CGWB)
facts.interpretation: 1 of Madurai district's 11 CGWB-assessed blocks (2024) is pumping faster than recharge; most stressed is Madurai West at 106% development. CGWB's pre-2023 rounds assessed 66 finer firka-level units, so earlier over-exploited counts are not directly comparable.

facts.title: Critical or semi-critical blocks
facts.interpretation: Beyond the over-exploited tier, 1 block is 'Critical' (>90% draft) and 3 are 'Semi Critical' (>70%). These are the watch-list zones where TWAD / Madurai Corporation interventions need to start before they tip over.

facts.title: F-grade wards on the risk composite
facts.interpretation: 12 of Madurai's 100 wards score F (composite >80) on the 3-factor risk index (groundwater depth 50%, water-body density 20%, water-body health 30%). Highest risk: Ward 88 (SOUTH) at 90.7/100. 34 more wards score D.

facts.title: Shallow groundwater depth (CGWB Year Book wells)
facts.interpretation: Across Madurai's 21 CGWB Year Book observation wells (manually-measured dug wells in the shallow/phreatic aquifer), depth-to-water averages 5.1 m, reaching about 11.9 m at the deepest well. Each ward is matched to its nearest well for the risk composite; the network is too sparse for a true per-ward survey, so this is a coarse nearest-well estimate, not interpolated precision.
facts.source_label: CGWB Ground Water Year Book (TN & Puducherry), 2023-25 · nearest-well

facts.title: Vaigai BOD pollution gradient through Madurai
facts.interpretation: CPCB 2024 NWMP readings: BOD jumps from 3 mg/L upstream of Madurai (Sellur) to 4.2 mg/L downstream (Anuppanadi). Sewage outfalls and textile dyeing through the city push the river over the 3 mg/L drinkable-after-treatment threshold.

facts.title: Vaigai dissolved oxygen, downstream of Madurai
facts.interpretation: Latest CPCB NWMP reading at Vaigai D/S Madurai (2024). The 5 mg/L threshold is the cutoff for outdoor bathing and propagation of fish/wildlife under CPCB Class C. Just above threshold.

facts.title: Urban tank area lost to encroachment
facts.interpretation: 14 fully lost + 12 severely reduced urban tanks. Combined area swallowed: ~16.5 sq km, roughly 30% of Madurai's old city footprint. ~15k slum households now sit on former tank beds.
